**Triage** — graded `p2`, `bug` + `tooling`, `pm:queue`, routed `domain:devx`. (Applied and read back first.)

## ⭐ There are four scanners with this defect, not three

The card names `enclosingOpeners`, `sliceBalanced` and `scanTopLevel`. At `origin/main` `bd4aa4e`, `scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs` carries the identical quote-skip at **four** sites:

| function | decl | quote-skip |
|---|---|---|
| `scanTopLevel` | `:1134` | `:1141` |
| `enclosingOpeners` | `:1539` | `:1549` |
| `sliceBalanced` | `:1558` | `:1567` |
| **`splitTopLevel`** | **`:1576`** | **`:1585`** |

And `splitTopLevel`'s own docblock is the sharpest evidence in the whole card:

```js
/** Split on TOP-LEVEL commas — a nested call, generic or template keeps its own. */
export function splitTopLevel(args) {
```

It claims template-awareness — "a nested call, generic **or template** keeps its own" — and then implements the same seek-to-matching-backtick that cannot survive a nested template. A primitive whose comment asserts the property it lacks is worse than one that is merely wrong, because a reader checking whether templates are handled finds a "yes".

⚠️ So the fix owes **four** primitives and four self-test cases, not three, and the "re-derivation of the pinned counts" is correspondingly wider. Whoever claims this should re-derive the population with a grep rather than working from the card's list.

## Why `p2`

You are careful that nothing is wrong today: both unplaced `code:` positions in `automation.ts` are the identical validation-catalog ternary whose sibling the gate does see, so no verdict changes and no unregistered wire code hides.

What earns `p2` is the sentence you wrote, which is the finding:

> a count the gate prints as a total is really a floor, and nothing said so until now

and the one after it — `enclosingOpeners` returns `undefined` for both "genuinely inside a string" (correct) and "the scanner lost its place 400 lines ago" (a defect), **and the caller cannot tell which**. 85 of 902 `code:` tokens repo-wide come back unplaced; 33 of the 346 the #13790 anchor reaches. Nobody can currently say how many of those are the second kind.

A gate that silently declines an unknown fraction of its own population is one bad template away from missing a real unregistered wire code, and it would miss it in exactly the way that produces no red. Not `p1` — nothing is red and nothing is unregistered today.

## Scope ruled

The template-literal mode (tracking `${` … `}` nesting rather than seeking a matching backtick) across **all four** primitives, plus:

⛔ **A `--self-test` case per primitive** with a nested-template fixture **and a positive control** — the control is the half that proves the fixture would have failed before. Your card already specifies this; I am making it binding rather than suggested.

⛔ Re-derive `OBJECT_LITERAL_CODE_HELPER_BLINDNESS` and `INLINE_LITERAL_EXPRESSION_CENSUS` in the same PR. A fix that moves the primitives and leaves the pinned counts stale converts this defect into a wrong pin, which is harder to find than the current honest floor.

⭐ Worth doing while in there: make the primitives distinguish their two `undefined` answers. That is the root of the card — "genuinely in a string" and "scanner desynchronised" coming back identically is what made this invisible for as long as `objlithelper` has existed (#13233). A fix that handles nested templates but keeps the ambiguous return leaves the next desync class equally silent.

⛔ Do not widen to `check:error-code-casing`. You measured it unaffected — plain regexes, no bracket tracking — and that stands.

## On the filing

Filing under Prime Directive #10 rather than folding it into PR #14625 was right: this is a change to three (four) shared primitives that every shape and every census figure in the gate depends on, and it cannot ride a shape widening. Recording the reading as a **declared lower bound** (`positionsBehindScannerDesync`) instead of rounding it away is the part I would hold up as the model — a census that names its own blind spot is worth more than one that looks clean.
